page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m1.2xlarge is an x86_64 instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, featuring 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 33 MB of shared L3 cache. Supported instruction sets include AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. The instance provides 8.0 GB of total RAM, creating a 1:1 ratio of 1.0 GB memory per vCPU. Hardware accelerators are absent, local storage is listed as none, and the system relies on a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results highlight solid multi-core instruction processing alongside lower single-threaded metrics. The instance achieves a PassMark CPU score of 6,910.95 and an extended instructions score of 5,883.17, both placing in the middle 50% tier. Conversely, single-thread testing yields a Geekbench single-core score of 925.0 and single-threaded gzip compression of 19.03 GB/sec, placing in the bottom 10%. Memory throughput reaches 32.76 GB/sec on uncached large-block writes and 37.77 GB/sec on uncached reads. Small 135M parameter language model execution reaches 440.5 prompt tokens per second, but throughput declines to 9.83 tokens per second on medium 7B models.

The primary operational tradeoff of the ecs.u0.c1m1.2xlarge centers on its restrictive memory footprint. With only 1.0 GB of memory per core and zero local storage, memory-heavy workloads and large in-memory databases risk capacity saturation. However, the dedicated core allocation ensures predictable CPU availability for parallelized tasks. Measured application throughput includes 5.74 million Redis SET operations per second and 4.2 GB/sec static web serving throughput. The platform is best suited for compute-focused microservices, lightweight web servers, background batch processing, and CI/CD build agents requiring moderate compute density without substantial memory demands.
